transportBoundaries.boundary: Implemented as python3 scripts/ope.py agent-call returning one JSON envelope to stdout.
transportBoundaries.approvalGate: The dispatcher surfaces approval_required and does not bypass request policy.
transportBoundaries.credentialBoundary: No credentials are needed or accepted in local prompt-visible arguments.

transportBoundaries.boundary: Implemented locally as a stdio JSON-RPC scaffold exposing one tool per agent operation.
transportBoundaries.approvalGate: The MCP scaffold exposes validation, dry-run, read, status, and scoring tools only.
transportBoundaries.credentialBoundary: MCP credentials must stay in server configuration, not tool arguments or records.

transportBoundaries.boundary: Future HTTP endpoints should keep OPE record semantics and map status from envelope exit codes.
transportBoundaries.approvalGate: Effectful, paid, live-fetch, or privacy-sensitive requests must be approval-gated.
transportBoundaries.credentialBoundary: HTTP credentials must be transport metadata, not forecast artifacts or provenance text.

transportBoundaries.boundary: Future queues should use request messages plus an ope.agent_envelope.ready result envelope.
transportBoundaries.approvalGate: Queued jobs must persist approval state and reject stale or unapproved effectful work.
transportBoundaries.credentialBoundary: Worker credentials must be scoped server-side and excluded from queued payloads.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs a compact probability before taking a reversible downstream action.
decisionExamples.reason: The card includes probability, baseline, status, request binding, and claim warnings.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Act only when caller policy accepts the quality boundary and resolution status.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs audit context or wants to explain what evidence supported the forecast.
decisionExamples.reason: The trace links the evidence plan, source policy, source set, connector registry, connector results, and gathered source records.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the trace for provenance inspection, not as proof that all possible internet evidence was gathered.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs the full forecast lifecycle for audit or explanation.
decisionExamples.reason: The bundle contains bound lifecycle records, evidence, history, resolution, and scoring context.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the bundle for audit context, not as a separate source of forecast semantics.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to understand the first safe setup action for a private setup request.
decisionExamples.reason: The bundle joins request, first-action, and runbook guidance without executing source setup.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the bundle as setup guidance only; do not treat it as a forecast or source-intake artifact.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs the full private setup adapter sequence before calling setup operations.
decisionExamples.reason: The runbook lists setup guidance, source-builder, source-handoff, method-gate, forecast execution, and normal readback order.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the runbook as read-only guidance; it must not execute adapter calls or create source, forecast, resolution, or scoring artifacts.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs compact private setup adapter conformance status before deciding which adapter operation to call.
decisionExamples.reason: The summary records phase counts, operation coverage, artifact boundaries, sanitized-error coverage, and the full matrix pointer without embedding every envelope.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the summary for routine conformance checks; load the full matrix only when implementing or debugging adapter behavior.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to know which private source kinds OPE can currently route before setup.
decisionExamples.reason: The guidance joins capability declarations, outcome classes, and intake-bridge routing without executing source reads.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use this as source-kind guidance only; planned private API, database, and upload paths remain non-executing.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to choose the next private source-kind path before lower-level setup calls.
decisionExamples.reason: The examples bind source adapter guidance, first actions, and the adapter-chain runbook into source-kind-specific next actions.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use these examples as read-only path selection; do not execute source setup, fixture evidence, forecasts, or scoring from this operation.

decisionExamples.situation: The private setup bundle says caller-approved local files are the next setup step.
decisionExamples.reason: The adapter inspects explicit CSV/JSON paths and returns draft manifest and mapping guidance.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Do not forecast from drafts until source intake, method gates, and benchmark decisions pass.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to continue from source-builder guidance into source-handoff next actions.
decisionExamples.reason: The adapter returns checked handoff status, mapping confirmation, intake binding, and method-gate readiness.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Only confirmed accepted handoffs may proceed to setup benchmark and method gates; the adapter itself does not forecast.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to know whether a confirmed private setup may run explicit forecast execution.
decisionExamples.reason: The adapter returns setup benchmark, method decision, selected method, and explicit forecast-execution readiness.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Run setup forecast execution only when the method gate recommends it; the adapter itself does not create forecasts.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent has method-gate permission and needs the setup forecast artifacts.
decisionExamples.reason: The adapter returns a setup forecast run plus forecast artifacts only for the allowed confirmed handoff.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the returned forecastId and questionId with forecast_card, lifecycle_bundle, resolution_status, or scoring_summary; do not invent a private setup read API.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to know whether any forward-run forecasts are due for outcome resolution.
decisionExamples.reason: The registry exposes pending, due, waiting, resolved, and invalid job guidance without executing resolvers.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use due job commands only after explicit live resolver approval; the readback itself must not execute.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs the latest scheduler status before deciding to wait, execute, inspect, or stop.
decisionExamples.reason: The status payload exposes the latest tick, queue states, shutdown/log path, execution mode, and next action.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Use the status as read-only guidance; it must not start a scheduler, execute resolvers, or create outcomes.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to know whether a forecast has resolved before scoring or waiting.
decisionExamples.reason: Resolution status is smaller than a full bundle and carries source and quality-claim status.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Do not score unresolved, ambiguous, annulled, or missing outcomes as normal resolved forecasts.

decisionExamples.situation: The agent needs to compare the forecast to a baseline before using it in a decision.
decisionExamples.reason: Scoring summary exposes scoring rule, primary score, baseline score, and quality boundary.
decisionExamples.downstreamRule: Do not generalize one fixture score into a live calibration or state-of-the-art claim.

warnings: The MCP stdio adapter is a local scaffold, not a hosted or production adapter runtime.
HTTP and queue mappings are not implemented runtimes.
Protocol adapters must preserve OPE record semantics and envelope exit codes.
Paid, effectful, live-fetch, or privacy-sensitive forecast requests remain approval-gated.
Do not place secrets in forecast artifacts, provenance metadata, tool arguments, or queued payloads.
